task: Coronary blood flow & autoregulation CERT: myocardial-perfusion SUPPLY-SIDE (distinct from cardiac-output/CICR/athlete-heart DEMAND-side certs already built). Five falsifiable claims, each with a forced adversary: (A) LV coronary flow is diastolic-dominant (Gregg-type phasic pattern, systolic wall-compression/vascular-waterfall mechanism) while RV differs (lower RV systolic pressure -> much weaker compression -> flow far more even across the cycle) -- a 'flow follows aortic driving pressure, peaks in systole' adversary must FAIL for LV specifically; (B) resting coronary O2 extraction is already near-maximal (~70-80%), so a further ~6x O2-demand rise must be met ~5x by FLOW not extraction, contrasted against a systemic/skeletal-muscle-like bed with substantial extraction headroom; (C) coronary flow is actively autoregulated (held closer to constant than a pressure-passive vessel) across ~60-140mmHg, using a REAL measured autoregulatory gain (not an assumed-flat idealization); (D) stenosis severity exhausts flow reserve (CFR/FFR) before resting flow itself collapses -- a naive 'flow falls linearly/purely-anatomically with %-diameter stenosis, no reserve buffer' adversary must fail against a physiology-based (flow-reserve) definition of significance, with real long-term clinical-outcome trials as the dysfunction-pole anchor; (E) tachycardia shortens the diastolic filling time DISPROPORTIONATELY (not just proportionally), reducing the subendocardial-viability ratio (SEVR=DPTI/TTI, Buckberg) and predisposing to subendocardial-first ischemia.

gates_summary.claim_A_phasic_flow_9_gates: ALL PASS -- naive chamber-blind adversary predicts systolic-dominant flow for BOTH chambers (ratio 0.686), which is directionally WRONG for the real LV (measured LAD ratio 2.85, diastolic-dominant) but much LESS wrong for the real RV (measured RCA ratio 1.35); the vascular-waterfall geometric model (Downey & Kirk 1975 mechanism + standard LV/RV chamber pressures + the twin's own aortic p_sys/p_dia) correctly orders derived_LV_ratio(67.2, idealization-inflated) >> derived_RV_ratio(0.84), matching the real data's ordering (LAD 2.85 >> RCA 1.35); both real ratios clear Olinger & Buckberg 1976's own independently-derived clinical thresholds (LAD 74.0% diastolic > their 60% LV-supply threshold; RCA 42.6% systolic > their 40% RV-territory threshold) -- a genuine cross-study replication spanning 31 years (1976 intraoperative flow-probe, n=100, vs 2007 intracoronary Doppler-wire, n=24).
gates_summary.claim_B_o2_extraction_3_gates: ALL PASS -- extraction-alone void-floor (ceiling 95%/rest 75% = 1.267x) cannot meet the real ~6x O2-demand rise; the flow-rise this arithmetic FORCES (4.74x) lands within 5.3% of the independently-reported real flow-rise (5x, Duncker & Bache 2008) -- a genuine, non-fitted over-determination. The coronary bed's extraction headroom (1.267x) is markedly smaller than the twin's own systemic/whole-body a-vO2diff headroom (2.636x, from blood_oxygen_transport.py's real rest-to-walking a-vO2diff), a decorrelated cross-layer confirmation of the LV-vs-generic-tissue asymmetry Duncker & Bache describe qualitatively for LV-vs-RV.
gates_summary.claim_C_autoregulation_4_gates: ALL PASS -- using Berwick 2012's REAL measured gain (Gc=0.46+/-0.11, not an assumed-flat idealization), the modeled flow variation across 60-140mmHg (0.457, on a fractional F/F0 scale) sits strictly between a pressure-passive void-floor (0.857) and an idealized-perfect-flat curve (0.0) -- autoregulation is real, partial, and quantified, not asserted as flat. Berwick's own experimentally-tested CPP range (40-140mmHg) covers the task's pre-registered 60-140mmHg range.
gates_summary.claim_D_stenosis_cfr_ffr_7_gates: ALL PASS -- Pijls 1996's own reported sensitivity/specificity (88%/100%) is independently machine-re-derived from its own raw counts (87.5%/100%, matching to <1pp); Wilson 1991's real, same-patient, head-to-head comparison shows a purely-anatomic (60%-diameter) stenosis definition is a SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE (P<0.05) predictor of real exercise-induced ischemia than a physiologic (CFR-based) definition; real diseased-vessel CFVR (de Bruyne 1996, ~1.4-1.9) sits below Wilson 1991's independently-derived normal CFR cutoff (>=3.5); DEFER's 5-year AND 15-year real clinical-outcome data both show the reserve-preserved (FFR>=0.75) state is durably benign, while reserve-exhausted (FFR<0.75) carries significantly worse 5-year outcomes (P=0.003); FAME 2009's RCT (n=1005) shows FFR-guided (<=0.80) treatment beats angiography-alone (13.2% vs 18.3% 1yr composite, P=0.02); FFR is ~4x more reproducible than CFVR (de Bruyne 1996, CoV 4.2% vs 17.7%). The 0.75-vs-0.80 FFR-threshold difference across sources is disclosed as a real historical evolution (original research validation vs modern guideline-adopted treatment cutoff), not smoothed over.
gates_summary.claim_E_tachycardia_subendocardial_6_gat: ALL PASS -- 4/4 active pharmacologic arms in Boudoulas 1979 show significant %-diastole change (P<0.05 to P<0.001) while the lidocaine arm (a genuine within-study null control, no HR/QS2 effect) shows none; the isoproterenol arm is the sharpest single test -- HR rises AND systole (QS2) itself shortens, yet %-diastole still DECREASES (56.1%->53.5%, P<0.05), proving diastole shrinks MORE than proportionally, not just proportionally. Chemla 2008 (n=203) shows real, tonometrically-measured SEVR is governed by cycle TIMING (r2 vs DT/ST=0.89, r2 vs HR=0.56, P<0.001) and NOT by absolute pressure level (explicitly NS vs systolic time/pulse pressure/mean pressures). Saito 2003 (n=178) independently confirms high pulse rate as one of several real risk factors for low SEVR. Chemla's (1.39) and Saito's (1.40) resting-SEVR magnitudes agree to within 15%, two independent human cohorts/methods/decades.

symmetric_qc_open_items: Claim A's derived LV diastole:systole ratio (67.2) is an idealization ARTIFACT of the open-aortic-valve equal-pressure assumption flooring the systolic denominator near zero -- the DIRECTION and ORDERING conclusions (LV >> RV) are load-bearing; the exact magnitude is explicitly NOT claimed as a precision prediction.

Graziosi 2007 (the primary human LAD-vs-RCA phasic-ratio source) is an advanced non-ischemic-cardiomyopathy cohort (n=24), not healthy controls -- disclosed; the qualitative/quantitative LAD>>RCA contrast itself is independently replicated in a DIFFERENT, healthy-adjacent intraoperative cohort (Olinger & Buckberg 1976, n=100, 1976) using a different method (flow-probe vs Doppler-wire) and different threshold convention (>60%D / >40%S vs a continuous ratio) -- the cross-study agreement is the load-bearing evidence, not either source alone.

The systemic a-vO2diff headroom comparator (Claim B) reused from blood_oxygen_transport.py is a whole-body MIXTURE (skeletal-muscle-dominated), used explicitly as a PROXY/analogy for Duncker & Bache's qualitative 'RV is similar to skeletal muscle' statement -- NOT a direct RV-coronary-sinus measurement; no such live-verified primary RV-specific extraction number was found this session.
